title: 3.2.6 Lab: shout(word)
description: Write a one-parameter function, shout, that prints its word in capital letters, then call it with two different words. Practice, not graded: the checks call your function.

steps.title: Write the function
steps.instructions: Write a function declaration called shout with one parameter, word, as in 3.2.5.

steps.title: Print the word in capitals
steps.instructions: Inside shout, use console.log to print word in capital letters with .toUpperCase() (1.2.14). This function prints its answer; return is first taught later, at 3.2.11.

steps.title: Call it twice
steps.instructions: Below the function, call shout with two different words, such as shout("hello") and shout("watch out"), and read the output.

requirements.title: shout is defined with one parameter
requirements.description: Code defines a function named shout with exactly one parameter. Help: 3.2.5 (Parameters and Arguments)
requirements.hint: Write function shout(word) { ... } with exactly that name and one name between the parentheses.

requirements.title: shout turns the word into capitals
requirements.description: shout uses .toUpperCase() in its body. Help: 1.2.14 (String Methods in Practice)
requirements.hint: Put .toUpperCase() after the parameter's name inside shout, like word.toUpperCase().

requirements.title: shout is called
requirements.description: Code calls shout at least once. Help: 3.2.5 (Parameters and Arguments)
requirements.hint: Add a line below the function that calls it, such as shout("hello");

requirements.title: shout prints the word in capitals
requirements.description: shout(word) prints the word in capital letters, whatever word it is given. Help: 1.2.14 (String Methods in Practice)
requirements.hint: shout must print the word in capitals with console.log, exactly one line. Check that you print word.toUpperCase(), not word, and that you print it once.
